title: Unified compute-credit ledger: mapping multi-product usage to invoiceable units and dispute resolution acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Customers use a mix of Redwood products (chat, embeddings, reranking, dedicated compute) and receive separate line items or confusing charge units. This leads to invoice disputes, unclear unit economics, and support load to reconcile usage across products. Goal: define a single, auditable compute-credit ledger that maps heterogeneous usage events into a unified invoiceable unit ("compute credits"), with deterministic conversion rules, near-real-time preview, and a defined dispute/resolution workflow.
background: Existing pricing artifacts cover per-route quotas, burst credits, and per-model compute mappings, but we lack a canonical conversion table and ledger model for cross-product billing. Several enterprise customers requested consolidated invoices and clearer per-feature attribution during Dedicated + Hosted mixed deployments. This PRD defines requirements for the ledger, rounding/aggregation rules, preview APIs, and acceptance criteria for billing accuracy and dispute handling.
requirements: Define canonical compute-credit unit (CCU) and conversion factors for all product primitives (token-generation, streaming tokens, embedding vector units, rerank calls, dedicated GPU-minute). Conversion factors must be defensible and versioned.
Ledger model: immutably record consumption events mapped to CCUs with metadata: timestamp, tenant, route, model-version, conversion-factor-id, raw-metrics (tokens, vectors), and campaign tags.

Near-real-time preview API (read-only) that returns current period CCU totals and per-route breakdown with confidence band for pending events (<=1% variance target for hosted workloads under normal ingestion).

Invoice generation: aggregate CCUs by billing window, apply customer plan entitlements (included CCUs, overage rates, discounts), and emit human-readable breakdown lines and machine-readable ledger export (CSV/NDJSON).

Rounding and fairness policy: rounding must happen only at the invoice line-item level (round to two decimals of currency) while CCU arithmetic must use fixed-point arithmetic (micro-CCUs) to avoid rounding drift across aggregation levels.

Retroactive plan changes: define algorithm for credits/refunds if customer downgrades and requests retroactive adjustments (max lookback 30 days) — include pro-rata carry-forward and audit log entries.

Dispute & adjustments workflow: support tagging ledger entries as disputed, hold corresponding invoice amount in a temporary dispute bucket, and allow automated reconciliation once dispute is resolved with audit trail.
Backward compatibility: support mapping legacy per-token and per-embedding invoices to CCUs for at least one historical year to enable customer audits.
Billing performance: invoice generation must complete within SLA: <10s for small accounts (<1M CCU) and <5m for large accounts (<1B CCU) in background processing, with streaming job status updates.
Admin UX: Console view for finance admins showing CCU breakdown, delta from previous billing period, and one-click export for accounting teams.
Security & audit: all ledger writes must be tamper-evident and accessible via read-only audit endpoints; KMS-encrypted at rest, with retention policy configurable per customer (default 1 year).
acceptance_criteria: Conversion table published with documented rationale and a version identifier; conversion tests covering edge cases for each product primitive exist and pass in CI.
Ledger event schema validated end-to-end: ingestion -> CCU mapping -> storage. Spot checks show no more than 0.1% missing fields over a 48-hour test window.
Preview API returns values within 1% of final invoice CCU totals for test workloads representing 3 defined load profiles (low-latency chat, batch embeddings, mixed dedicated bursts).
Sample invoices generated for three tenants (startup, mid-market, enterprise) and manually reviewed by finance for clarity and traceability; all line-items map to ledger IDs.
Rounding policy demonstrably avoids drift: synthetic test with repeated aggregations over 1,000 simulated accounts shows invoice totals equal to ledger-sum (±$0.01 per account).

Dispute flow: simulate a disputed ledger entry, ensure dispute hold reduces payable amount on the invoice, and that resolution pathways (adjust, waive, refund) create audit entries and adjust the next billing cycle accordingly.
Performance: invoice generation SLA met in staging for small and large account targets; telemetry logged and dashboards created for monitoring.
Security: ledger encryption and audit endpoints implemented and reviewed by security; access controls prevent write operations from non-authorized services in test environment.
Rollout plan approved by billing, finance, solutions engineering, and legal stakeholders.
Customer-facing docs drafted: mapping guide, FAQ, and dispute SLA published in support docs.
test_cases: TC1 - Token to CCU mapping: generate 1M chat tokens across various models and verify CCU equals expected using conversion table v1.2.
TC2 - Embedding rounding: run 10k embedding requests with fractional CCUs and assert invoice-level rounding only at currency step.
TC3 - Retroactive downgrade: simulate plan downgrade with 20k CCU consumption in prior window and verify refund calculation and ledger audit entries.
TC4 - Dispute lifecycle: open dispute on three entries, validate hold behavior, close disputes with mixed outcomes (partial refund, credit, reject) and check invoice adjustments.
TC5 - Preview accuracy: run sustained load for 24h and assert preview API deviation <=1% from final computation.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design & signoff (2 sprints): finalize conversion table, ledger schema, and acceptance criteria.
Phase 1 - Minimal viable ledger (1 sprint): ingest events for hosted API and emit CCU totals; no invoice binding.
Phase 2 - Preview API & console (2 sprints): expose read-only preview to sample customers and internal finance users.
Phase 3 - Billing integration (2 sprints): wire ledger into invoice generator and create CSV/NDJSON exports for accounting.
Phase 4 - Pilot customers (4 weeks): onboard 3 pilot customers (one from each segment) for validation and feedback.
Phase 5 - GA & migration (6 weeks): enable default for new customers, opt-in for existing customers, monitor for disputes and support load.
metrics: Number of billing-related support tickets <= 10% of prior baseline after GA
open_questions: Do we expose conversion-factor versions to customers or only show derived CCU numbers?
What is the maximum lookback window finance/legal will accept for retroactive adjustments?
Should prepaid plans burn down in CCUs or remain as monetary balance with CCU equivalence?
Do partners/resellers require a secondary mapping schema for partner margins?
notes: This spec intentionally separates the ledger model (single source of truth for consumption) from invoice presentation. Early engineering work should prioritize the immutable ledger and conversion determinism to keep later accounting work straightforward. Finance must be engaged before Phase 3 to validate edge-case handling for credits/refunds.
